correctness.rationale: For zero-sum vectors the full powered distance form equals minus the squared Euclidean norm plus 2(2^p-1) times the product of two exclusive-clique sums. Orthogonal decomposition leaves a 2x2 quadratic form with positive diagonal, whose determinant gives the threshold and one-dimensional critical kernel. Explicit constant-group vectors prove failure above threshold. Integer rearrangement proves the 1-negative-type criterion and an exhaustive elementary N<=9 argument proves the first two counterexamples. The independent full-vertex rational Gram checker passed 1,320 tests, and 10,469 p=1 comparisons; finite testing is corroboration, not the infinite proof.
